identity.name: Cyclamic acid and its sodium/calcium salts (cyclamates)

function.mechanism: Provides strong sweet taste at low concentrations (reported around 30-40 times sucrose) without nutritive sugar load.

adi.basis: Latest EFSA sweeteners topic page lists E952 as re-evaluation ongoing and does not provide a completed EFSA E952 ADI conclusion.

efsa.key_finding: E952 is listed among sweeteners authorised in the EU, with EFSA re-evaluation still ongoing as of the latest EFSA topic update.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA cyclamic acid entry reports ADI 0-11 mg/kg bw.

notable_bans: United States: direct addition/use in human food prohibited under 21 CFR 189.135.

concerns.summary: A 2022 mouse model study reported dose- and time-related liver injury with inflammatory markers, plus heart/kidney injury signals at high intraperitoneal sodium cyclamate doses.

A 2025 rat ex vivo study found cyclohexylamine (cyclamate metabolite) contracts vas deferens via adrenergic pathways, indicating biologically plausible reproductive-system pharmacology concerns under experimental conditions.
Historical carcinogenic concern exists, but current IARC classification for cyclamates (sodium cyclamate) is Group 3 and recent reviews report no consistent human carcinogenic signal.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC classifies cyclamates (sodium cyclamate entry) as Group 3.
JECFA retains an ADI framework of 0-11 mg/kg bw for cyclamic acid/cyclamates.

populations: high consumers of cyclamate-sweetened beverages/tabletop sweeteners
adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA 2009 comments indicate exceedance risk for high consumers (including children) at several higher maximum-use scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Cyclamates are still authorised in the EU with an ongoing EFSA re-evaluation and have a maintained JECFA ADI, but exposure caveats (including child/high-consumer exceedance scenarios) and experimental toxicity signals prevent a low-concern classification. IARC Group 3 and the lack of consistent human carcinogenic evidence argue against a high tier.
key_factors: EFSA lists E952 re-evaluation as ongoing while authorised in the EU.
FDA/eCFR classifies cyclamate use in human food as prohibited (21 CFR 189.135).
JECFA ADI is 0-11 mg/kg bw with 2009 exposure comments showing possible exceedance in high consumers/children at higher use levels.
IARC classifies cyclamates (sodium cyclamate) as Group 3.
Recent mechanistic/animal studies report toxicity signals primarily under high or experimental exposure conditions.
